label.summary: These claims primarily concern critiques of capitalism, focusing on its exploitative nature and the pursuit of alternatives. Several claims advocate for shifting power and resources away from corporate elites and towards ordinary people, and envision a future without for-profit systems for essential services. The claims also address the need for worker self-organization and democratic control of wealth.
label.title: Critiques and Alternatives to Capitalism

claims.claim_text: The President says that capitalism without competition isn't capitalism, it's exploitation.
In overcoming the order of capitalism, the working class will not only liberate itself from its own shackles, but all of humanity from the parasitic death-drive of capitalism.
Support for others to rally to the cause of fighting crony capitalism.
Neoliberal capitalist austerity policies enacted by governments the world over, including Wall Street Democrats in the U.S., force poor and working people to compete with each other to survive.
Support for freedom of working-class self-organization and democratic political action.
Workers deserve better living conditions than capitalism provides.
In a future without capitalism, food, education, energy, medicine, and transportation may not be for-profit businesses.
Working people can only truly govern their destiny when they achieve democratic control of the wealth their labor (paid and unpaid) creates by building a democratic socialist society.

As socialists, the group fights for the right to economic self-determination against a system in which access to the labor market affects the ability to secure stable housing, food, medical care, and so many other human rights.
Commitment to challenge attacks of neoliberal capitalist austerity on the rights and freedoms of citizens.
In the near term, democratic socialists struggle for reforms that shift power and resources away from corporate elites and put them in the hands of ordinary people.
A capitalist system exploits workers instead of benefiting them.
